cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to God's people in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's just told them sin shall not be their master, because they're not under law, but under grace (Romans 6:14). So he asks the question somebody was bound to ask: "Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace?"

cards.question: Paul asks if we should keep sinning since we're under grace and not under law. What's his answer?

cards.text: Friend, that's like me hearing every burnt batch is forgiven and cranking every oven to MAXIMUM just to celebrate. Then Paul explains with a picture he says they should already know: slaves and masters.

cards.question: In Paul's picture of slaves and masters, who does he say you're a slave to?

answers.text: The one you were born under

cards.question: Paul says that besides being a slave to sin or to obedience, there's a third option: offering yourself to no master at all.
Paul says each master takes you somewhere. You're a slave either to sin leading to ___, or to obedience leading to ___.

cards.text: Then Paul stops to give thanks to God. These folks in Rome once were slaves to sin, but that's not where their story stayed.

cards.question: The believers in Rome were once slaves to sin. What does Paul thank God that they did?

answers.text: Kept every part of the law
Worked to earn their own freedom

cards.question: Paul says that once the believers in Rome were set free from sin, they had no master at all.

cards.text: Set free from sin, they've become slaves to righteousness, and then Paul says, "I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh." I respect that, friend, because when anybody explains anything to me, I need it in cookie terms or I'm LOST.

cards.question: Paul says the believers used to offer the parts of their body in slavery to impurity. What does he tell them to do with those same parts now?

answers.text: Offer them in slavery to righteousness
Keep them out of all service
Offer them back to the law

cards.question: They used to offer their bodies in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness. But Paul says slavery to righteousness leads to ___.

cards.text: Then Paul looks back: when they were slaves to sin, they were free of obligation to righteousness. That's like me bragging I'm free from my oven timer, friend, free to scrape charcoal off every tray I OWN.

cards.question: Paul asks what fruit they reaped back then from the things they're now ashamed of. What does he say the outcome of those things is?

cards.text: Then come two words I'd stamp on every cookie I own: but now. Paul says they've been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, and the fruit they reap leads to holiness.

cards.question: Paul says that for those who've been set free from sin and become slaves to God, the outcome is the same as it was before.

cards.text: Then Paul lands the whole thing with one line, and it starts on payday. Sin hands out a paycheck, friend, and trust me, you do NOT want to open that envelope.

cards.question: Paul puts what sin pays next to what God gives: the wages of sin is ___, but the ___ of God is eternal life.
Paul says eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord is something you earn, the same way you earn wages.
